what: Every entry of the OBITUARY printed in Robert Fergus's Directory of the City of Chicago for 1843 (1896) — names, trades, places, dates and ages at death of settlers and of other well-known citizens — read as it is printed, with the age kept verbatim beside the birth window it implies.
the_header_admission:
Names, places * , dates, and ages at death
of some of Chicago's Old Settlers, prior to 1843, and other well - known citizens who arrived after 1843, together
with others prominently connected with Illinois history:
what_the_admission_costs_this_list: Presence in this list is not evidence of arrival before 1843 and never evidence of residence on 1 July 1835. Gov. Richard Yates, Henry Ward Beecher and Morris Birkbeck of Edwards County are all printed here. What the list gives is a DATE: a death, and through the age an interval the birth falls in. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) that corroborates, enriches and dates; it never mints a resident and never lifts a grade.
the_place_default: * In most cases, except as otherwise stated, the deaths occurred in Chicago.
the_arithmetic: Every birth window is `inferred` and carries its own subtraction. An age printed to the day ('82-2-15') is exact; an age in years and months ('48-6', and the fractions '89½' and '24 2/3', which are months the volume elsewhere spells out) gives a window of a month; a bare age in years gives a window of a year and so two candidate birth years. Where the age is truncated in the transcription, hedged with 'about', or the death carries no year, no window is derived and the record says which.
